weather_line: Overcast in the corridor · owl-flight conditions: acceptable

stories.headline: Ashworth Replies: 'It Is a Room' — Three Words; No Further Elaboration; the Kitchen Table Has Not Moved Since
body: At six minutes past nine Tuesday morning, Mira Ashworth's owl arrived — a small, composed bird that landed on the sill, deposited a single folded square of burnt-sienna paper, and left without accepting a treat. The note read, in Ashworth's characteristically precise hand: 'It is a room.'

Christine read it twice. Steve read it once, set it down, and went to stand at the kitchen window for a moment. The sketch remains on the table. The unlabelled circle sits four millimetres above the shelf notation, as it always has, and now carries a provisional name: the Room. Ashworth did not say what kind of room. She did not say what is in it. She did not say whether she has been inside.

The expedition file has been updated. The run is being scheduled. The Jeep, informed of the development via the usual channels — a hand on the bonnet, a long pause — has reportedly offered no objection, which those familiar with the vehicle will understand as enthusiasm.

stories.headline: Longstanding Dispute Over Vault 612 Untangled in Full; the Goblins Shake Hands; One Appears Grateful, Which Is Unprecedented
body: A compound inheritance dispute affecting Vault 612 — open since approximately the second Quidditch World Cup and involving three branches of the Whitmore family, a sealed codicil, and a goblin records clerk who had misfiled the primary deed under a different century — was resolved Tuesday morning in a session lasting forty minutes.

Christine closed the file, capped her quill, and asked whether there were further questions. There were not. Griphook the Elder, who has attended eleven previous hearings on this matter and has never once been described as grateful, was described by three separate witnesses as grateful. He has not confirmed this and is not expected to.

stories.section: Ministry Watch · Subcommittee on Emerging Concerns
stories.headline: Subcommittee Learns of 'the Room'; Formally Petitions to Rename It Before Anyone Has Visited It; the Room Declines to Comment
body: The Ministry Subcommittee on Emerging Cartographic Concerns — which earlier this session claimed jurisdiction over geometric shapes found in the field, a claim still under internal review — has learned of Ashworth's three-word reply and convened an emergency lunchtime sitting to address it.

The subcommittee passed a motion to provisionally designate the feature 'Undifferentiated Elevated Enclosure (Corridor Region, Unverified)' pending formal survey, noting that the name 'the Room' had not been submitted through proper nomenclature channels. A counter-motion observing that the subcommittee does not own the corridor, the shelf, or Ashworth's vocabulary was tabled for Wednesday.

stories.headline: Lucy Reviews the Note; Ellie Asks Whether 'a Room' Means There Will Be a Sofa; Jersey Considers the Matter Settled
body: Sources within the household confirm that all three familiars were present when Ashworth's reply was read aloud. Reactions varied considerably by temperament and intellectual disposition.

Lucy is understood to have examined the note, scented the burnt-sienna ink — the same as the stamp, the same as the sketch — and retreated to her corner in a manner described by observers as 'satisfied but withholding.' She has made no statement. Ellie turned her head to one side upon hearing the word 'room,' then turned it to the other side, then asked, by means of sustained eye contact with the nearest biscuit tin, whether a room implied soft furnishings and the possibility of an afternoon nap. Jersey, curled on the window bench with the afternoon warmth on his back, is reported to have received the news calmly and returned to sleep within four seconds, which those close to him have interpreted as unconditional support for the expedition.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Has reviewed Ashworth's note, the sketch, and the updated expedition file, and declines to share her conclusions at this time; states only that she knew the corridor had more to offer and considers this a matter of public record.
Ellie: Has decided that 'a room' above Marker 9 very likely has a warm floor, a good smell, and possibly a second Ellie inside it, and is looking forward to meeting her.
Jersey: Remains on the window bench; has identified this as the warmest viable position in the northern hemisphere; is available for expedition support in a strictly advisory and lap-based capacity.
founding_editor_note: A room, is it. Well. First thing you do is check the ceiling height and whether anyone has bothered to square the corners — in my experience they never have. — D.

in_brief.sport: The Holyhead Harpies strength coach has reportedly reviewed Christine's Tuesday morning schedule and asked, with genuine professional interest, how she fits it all in; no answer was provided, as the morning was already over.
in_brief.forecast: Persistent overcast through the hollow; the Room remains unlabelled on all official charts; this is expected to continue until Saturday.

storyline_updates.title: Above Marker 9
storyline_updates.summary: Day 4: Ashworth's reply arrived at nine-oh-six Tuesday morning — three words: 'It is a room.' She did not elaborate on the type of room, its contents, or whether she has been inside. The unlabelled circle on the sketch is now provisionally called the Room. Steve has been informed; the Jeep has been informed; the expedition file has been updated with a run date pending. Day 5 should be the run itself: Christine and Steve drive the spur above Marker 9, make the shelf, and reach or glimpse the Room — a natural stone chamber, a clearing with walls, something that earns the name. The resolution should be warm and a little awe-struck, with a moment of Christine and Steve in it together, and perhaps a small final word from Ashworth confirming she knew it was worth finding.
